newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close a touch lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close a touch lower in quiet trade.

text.p: French stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday after a cautious day of moderate trading.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.17 points or 0.05 percent at 2,212.11. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 21 points at 1655 GMT. Volume for the day was 5.9 billion francs, with 4.3 billion on the CAC-40 index.
Trading was dominated by professionals, with little international interest in French stocks, dealers said.
In the later part of the session the market tracked Wall Street and lost some slight early gains.

Most traders expected the market to stay range bound on Friday barring a sharp drop in New York stocks or a surprise announcement by French President Jacques Chirac in his television appearance later tonight.
Presidential aides ruled out the announcement of a change of government or abrupt policy changes during the prime-time 90-minute broadcast beginning at 8.50 p.m. (1950 GMT).
Instead, they said Chirac hoped to win over sceptics by better explaining the long-term benefits of his austerity policies on the eve of a key European Union summit in Dublin.
In the meantime, U.S. market movements continue to provide the Paris bourse with its main direction, traders said.
"We are suspended on American rates, American data and on the direction of Wall Street," one said.
Retail stocks were busy Thursday, with activity boosted by Carrefour's Wednesday announcement of its purchase of a big stake in the company controlling the Cora retailing chain.
Casino and Promodes, widely rumoured to be potential merger candidates, were active but the companies both declined to make any comment on the persistent market talk.
Casino closed up 4.24 percent, the biggest gainer for the day, while Promodes -- viewed as Casino's most likely suitor -- ended down 0.43 percent.

Shares in Thomson SA defense electronics unit Thomson-CSF jumped 3.61 percent, the second biggest gain on the bourse on Thursday after the Finance Ministry's announcement on Wednesday night that it will relaunch its sale of Thomson, starting with the selloff of 58-percent owned Thomson-CSF.
The government said it would sell consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia at a later unspecified date.
"This solution has the merit of being clear, and concerns a company on which we can put a value," said Jean-Marc Buchet of brokers Ferri.
"There is little or no debt...the industrial asset is high quality," another analyst said about Thomson-CSF.
